rows.question: When does my maternity leave start if my due date is 15 November 2026?
rows.reply:
Mutterschutz (statutory maternity protection period) before the birth covers the last six weeks before the expected date of delivery. The law says the employer may not employ a pregnant woman "in den letzten sechs Wochen vor der Entbindung" (in the last six weeks before delivery). This is called the "Schutzfrist vor der Entbindung".

The six weeks are counted from the expected date of delivery shown on the certificate from a doctor, midwife or male midwife ("der voraussichtliche Tag der Entbindung … wie er sich aus dem ärztlichen Zeugnis oder dem Zeugnis einer Hebamme oder eines Entbindungspflegers ergibt"). With an expected date of 15 November 2026, counting six weeks back puts the start in early October 2026. The excerpts do not set out how the first day is counted.

During these six weeks you may still work, but only if you expressly declare that you are willing to. You can withdraw that declaration at any time, with effect for the future.

If the baby is not born on the expected date, the period before the birth becomes shorter or longer to match.

After the birth, the protection period lasts eight weeks. It is extended to twelve weeks:
1. for premature births,
2. for multiple births, and
3. if a doctor identifies a disability in the child before the eight weeks end. In this case the extension applies only if the mother applies for it.
If the baby is born early, the period after the birth is also extended by the time lost before the birth.

Mutterschaftsgeld is paid for the protection periods and for the day of delivery. For payments before the birth, the certificate stating the expected delivery date is what counts.

The Mutterschutz law does not cover self-employed women.

Your employer is bound by these protection periods. Your health insurance fund (Krankenkasse) handles Mutterschaftsgeld.

rows.question: How long after birth can we apply for Elterngeld without losing money?
rows.reply:
The law sets no fixed application deadline, but it limits how far back Elterngeld (parental allowance) is paid. Under BEEG §7(1), Elterngeld is paid retroactively only for the last three months of the child's life before the start of the month of life in which the application is received: "Es wird rückwirkend nur für die letzten drei Lebensmonate vor Beginn des Lebensmonats geleistet, in dem der Antrag auf Elterngeld eingegangen ist." Months of the child's life earlier than that are not paid. The same subsection says Elterngeld must be applied for in writing ("Elterngeld ist schriftlich zu beantragen").

Elterngeld can be received from the day of birth (BEEG §4(1): "Es kann ab dem Tag der Geburt bezogen werden"). So the later the application arrives, the more of the child's earliest months of life fall outside the three-month window and are lost.

The Elterngeldstelle responsible for your district decides on your individual application.

rows.question: How much notice do I have to give my employer for Elternzeit?
rows.reply:
Elternzeit (parental leave (unpaid job-protected leave)) is not applied for with an authority. You request it from your employer in writing, and the notice depends on when the leave falls (BEEG §16(1)).

- Leave before the child's third birthday: at least seven weeks before the leave starts ("spätestens sieben Wochen").
- Leave between the third birthday and the end of the child's eighth year: at least 13 weeks before the leave starts ("spätestens 13 Wochen").

The request must be made "in Textform". The official Familienportal explains that this can be a letter without a signature or an email.

When you request Elternzeit for the period before the third birthday, you must also state at the same time which periods within two years you will take as Elternzeit ("für welche Zeiten innerhalb von zwei Jahren"). For a mother whose Elternzeit follows directly after the maternity protection period, that period counts towards the two years.

The statute allows a shorter notice period only as an exception: "Bei dringenden Gründen ist ausnahmsweise eine angemessene kürzere Frist möglich" (for urgent reasons, an appropriate shorter period is possible). The Familienportal gives premature births as an example. It also says the length of the shorter period depends on the individual case.

A separate rule applies to mothers. If, for a reason that is not their fault, they could not request Elternzeit on time for leave directly after the maternity protection period, they can make the request within one week after that reason ends (BEEG §16(2)).

Your employer must confirm your Elternzeit to you in writing ("Der Arbeitgeber hat ... die Elternzeit zu bescheinigen").

Protection against dismissal starts from the time you request Elternzeit. It starts no earlier than eight weeks before leave taken before the third birthday, and no earlier than 14 weeks before leave between the third and eighth birthdays (BEEG §18(1)).

rows.question: How long is maternity protection after the birth if the baby comes early?
rows.reply:
Under MuSchG §3(2), the Mutterschutz (statutory maternity protection period) after the birth normally lasts eight weeks. The statute says "bis zum Ablauf von acht Wochen nach der Entbindung".

It is extended to twelve weeks in three cases:
1. premature births ("bei Frühgeburten"),
2. multiple births, and
3. where a disability in the child, within the meaning of §2(1) sentence 1 SGB IX, is medically established before eight weeks after the birth have passed. This third extension applies only if the woman applies for it.

If the baby arrives before the expected date, the period after the birth is also extended. It grows by the time the period before the birth was cut short. The statute says it "verlängert sich ... um den Zeitraum der Verkürzung der Schutzfrist vor der Entbindung". This applies to both the eight-week and the twelve-week period.

The period before the birth is six weeks. It is counted from the expected date of delivery shown in the certificate from a doctor or midwife (MuSchG §3(1)).

In practice this means:
- An early birth that is not medically a premature birth gives eight weeks after the birth plus the days lost before it. The Familienportal describes this as the total still being 14 weeks.
- A birth that counts as a premature birth gives twelve weeks after the birth plus the days lost before it.

The statute excerpt does not define "Frühgeburt". The Familienportal gives a birth weight under 2,500 grams as one example.

The twelve-week extension does not apply to a stillbirth (MuSchG §3(2), last sentence).

If your employer asks you to work during this period, the Familienportal says you can turn to your supervisory authority.

rows.question: Can my employer dismiss me while I am pregnant?
rows.reply:
In general, no. Under § 17 MuSchG, dismissal of a woman by her employer is unlawful ("Die Kündigung gegenüber einer Frau ist unzulässig") in three periods:

1. during her pregnancy;
2. until four months after a miscarriage after the twelfth week of pregnancy;
3. until the end of her protective period after the birth, and at least until four months after the birth.

This Kündigungsschutz (protection against dismissal) applies if the employer knows of the pregnancy, the miscarriage or the birth at the time of dismissal, or is told within two weeks after the dismissal is received ("innerhalb von zwei Wochen nach Zugang der Kündigung"). Missing the two weeks does no harm if the delay was for a reason the woman is not responsible for and she gives the notice without delay. The official guidance adds that the protection also applies if you did not yet know you were pregnant, but you must already have been pregnant when you received the dismissal.

There is one exception. The supreme Land authority responsible for occupational safety, or a body it designates, can exceptionally declare a dismissal permissible in special cases that are not connected with the woman's condition during pregnancy, after a miscarriage or after the birth. Such a dismissal must be in writing and must state the reason. The official guidance gives these as examples of such special cases: the company is insolvent; the business is partly closed down; in a small business, it cannot continue without a qualified replacement; or a particularly serious breach of duty. It also says that without the authority's approval the dismissal is invalid ("Ohne die Zustimmung der Aufsichtsbehörde ist die Kündigung unwirksam").

If you are dismissed without that approval, the guidance says you must bring a claim before the competent labour court, "normalerweise innerhalb von 3 Wochen" (normally within 3 weeks) from receiving the written dismissal. If you do not bring a claim, the dismissal counts as legally effective. You can bring the claim yourself, through a representative such as a lawyer, or orally at the court office. The guidance also says you should involve the responsible supervisory authority. If the authority did approve the dismissal, you can also challenge that approval, but this does not replace the labour court claim.

Whether a particular dismissal is permissible is decided by the occupational-safety authority of your Land, and its validity by the labour court.

rows.question: Is there an income limit above which we get no Elterngeld?
rows.reply:
Yes. The law sets an income limit above which there is no entitlement to Elterngeld (parental allowance).

BEEG §1(8) says the entitlement lapses ("Ein Anspruch entfällt") if the person earned a zu versteuerndes Einkommen (taxable income) of "mehr als 175 000 Euro" in the last completed tax assessment period before the child's birth ("im letzten abgeschlossenen Veranlagungszeitraum vor der Geburt des Kindes").

Where another person also meets the conditions, for example the other parent living in the same household with the child, the limit applies to both incomes added together. The entitlement lapses if "die Summe des zu versteuernden Einkommens beider Personen mehr als 175 000 Euro beträgt".

The limit refers to taxable income, not gross income. The federal guidance page notes that taxable income is usually considerably lower than gross income, and that the Finanzamt determines it and states it in the tax assessment (Steuerbescheid).

If the tax assessment for that period is not yet available when you apply, and it cannot yet be said whether the limit is exceeded, BEEG §8(3) says the amount is decided provisionally on the basis of the information you have credibly stated ("vorläufig").

The 175,000 euro figure is what the statute in these excerpts states. The guidance page describes different limits for earlier births. The transitional provision governing earlier births is not among these excerpts, so I cannot state which limit applies to a birth before that change.

Whether the limit affects your family is decided by the Elterngeldstelle for your district, not by this service.

rows.question: How many months of Elterngeld can we get in total?
rows.reply:
Elterngeld (parental allowance) comes in two forms: basic Elterngeld and Elterngeld Plus. The month counts below are set by BEEG §4.

The basic allowance: parents together are entitled to 12 monthly amounts ("Die Eltern haben gemeinsam Anspruch auf zwölf Monatsbeträge Basiselterngeld"). They are entitled to 2 further months, called partner months, if one parent's income from work is reduced in two months of the child's life ("zwei weitere Monate Basiselterngeld (Partnermonate)"). That makes 14 months of the basic allowance at most for a child born on time.

Swapping for Elterngeld Plus: instead of one month of the basic allowance, a parent can take two months of Elterngeld Plus ("jeweils zwei Lebensmonate Elterngeld Plus").

The partnership bonus: on top of this, each parent can receive at most four monthly amounts of the partnership bonus under BEEG §4b ("höchstens vier zustehenden Monatsbeträge Partnerschaftsbonus"). The official Familienportal describes this as up to 4 additional months of Elterngeld Plus each, when both parents work part-time at the same time. The full conditions are in §4b, which is not among the sources here.

Limits per parent:
- One parent can receive at most 12 monthly amounts of the basic allowance, plus the partnership bonus.
- A parent is only entitled to Elterngeld if they take it for at least two months of the child's life.
- Months in which a mother receives maternity benefits counted under BEEG §4(4) are treated as months of the basic allowance.

Time windows: Elterngeld is paid for months of the child's life, not calendar months.
- The basic allowance can be received until the child completes the 14th month of life.
- Elterngeld Plus can be received until the child completes the 32nd month of life. From the 15th month, at least one parent must take it in consecutive months.

Premature births: the joint total of the basic allowance is higher for a child born early, measured from the expected delivery date in the doctor's or midwife's certificate.
- At least 6 weeks early: 13 monthly amounts.
- At least 8 weeks early: 14 monthly amounts.
- At least 12 weeks early: 15 monthly amounts.
- At least 16 weeks early: 16 monthly amounts.
In these cases the per-parent maximum and the age windows are extended correspondingly.

How many months your family actually receives depends on how you split the months and which conditions you meet. Only the Elterngeldstelle for your district decides that.

rows.question: What is the Partnerschaftsbonus and who qualifies?
rows.reply:
The Partnerschaftsbonus (partnership bonus months) gives each parent extra monthly payments of parental allowance when both work part-time at the same time. The statute calls it an additional monthly amount of the Plus variant of parental allowance: "einen zusätzlichen Monatsbetrag Elterngeld Plus (Partnerschaftsbonus)" (BEEG §4b(1)).

Conditions in the law (BEEG §4b):
- Both parents work at least 24 and at most 32 hours a week, on average over the child's month of life ("nicht weniger als 24 und nicht mehr als 32 Wochenstunden im Durchschnitt des Lebensmonats").
- Both parents meet the conditions of BEEG §1. The excerpts do not set out what §1 requires.
- Each parent can receive at most four monthly amounts, and only if they take it for at least two months of life.
- Both parents must take it at the same time, in consecutive months of life.

If, while you are receiving it, one parent comes to meet one of the grounds for sole receipt in BEEG §4c(1) nos. 1 to 3, one parent can continue receiving it alone (BEEG §4b(4)).

One parent alone (BEEG §4c(2)). A parent can claim these extra monthly amounts alone, for two to four consecutive months of life, working 24 to 32 hours a week on average, if any one of these three grounds applies:
1. the parent meets the conditions for the tax relief for single parents (§24b(1) and (3) of the Income Tax Act), and the other parent lives neither with them nor with the child;
2. care by the other parent would endanger the child's welfare within the meaning of §1666(1) and (2) of the Civil Code;
3. care by the other parent is impossible, in particular because of a serious illness or a severe disability. Economic reasons and being busy with other activities do not count.

If the conditions turn out not to have been met in every month applied for, the requirement of consecutive months is still treated as met (BEEG §4b(5)). The federal guidance page adds that if you work outside the 24 to 32 hour range in a month, the bonus for that month must be repaid, and if only one parent misses the condition, both lose the bonus for that month.

Amount. The federal guidance page says the bonus is calculated the same way as the Plus variant and is between 150 and 900 euros per parent per month, depending on income before the birth.

Whether you qualify, and how much you would receive, is decided by the Elterngeldstelle responsible for your district.

rows.question: We forgot to apply for Kindergeld. How far back will they pay?
rows.reply:
Kindergeld (child benefit) is paid backdated for at most six months. The law says payment is made "rückwirkend nur für die letzten sechs Monate vor Beginn des Monats, in dem der Antrag auf Kindergeld eingegangen ist". That means only the six months before the start of the month in which the Familienkasse receives the application. Earlier months are not paid out.

The same section also says the entitlement itself is not affected by this payment limit ("Der Anspruch auf Kindergeld nach § 62 bleibt von dieser Auszahlungsbeschränkung unberührt"). What is limited is how far back money is paid out.

Because the six months are counted back from the month the application arrives, each month that passes before it arrives means one more earlier month is not paid.

Kindergeld must be applied for in writing, and the application should be made to the responsible Familienkasse. The official family portal says you should state in the application that you are applying retroactively and from when you want to receive Kindergeld. It also says to submit the application to the Familienkasse at your Agentur für Arbeit.

Whether you are entitled, and for which months you are paid, is decided by the Familienkasse.

rows.question: How much Kindergeld do we get per month for our first child?
rows.reply:
Kindergeld (child benefit) is set by federal law as a flat monthly amount per child. The statute reads: "Das Kindergeld beträgt monatlich für jedes Kind 259 Euro". That is 259 euros per month for each child. The law sets the same figure for every child, so it does not give a separate amount for a first child. The same sentence appears in both the Einkommensteuergesetz (§66) and the Bundeskindergeldgesetz (§6).

The law also says when payment runs: "vom Beginn des Monats an ..., in dem die Anspruchsvoraussetzungen erfüllt sind, bis zum Ende des Monats, in dem die Anspruchsvoraussetzungen wegfallen". That means payment runs from the start of the month in which the conditions are met until the end of the month in which they stop being met. The law ties the amount to future increases in the child tax allowances ("Freibeträge für Kinder"). If those allowances are raised, Kindergeld is raised to match.

This is the rule the law sets. Whether your family is entitled is decided by the Familienkasse, not by this service. The federal family portal links to the online Kindergeld application at the Bundesagentur für Arbeit.

rows.question: How quickly do we have to register the birth at the Standesamt?
rows.reply:
The birth must be reported to the Standesamt (civil registry office) responsible for the place where the child was born within one week. The statute says "binnen einer Woche anzuzeigen" (to be reported within one week). It can be reported by the persons the law names, orally or in writing, or in writing by the institutions it names. If a child is stillborn, the report must be made at the latest on the third working day after the birth ("spätestens am dritten auf die Geburt folgenden Werktag").

The federal family portal explains that when a child is born in a hospital, birth centre or maternity clinic, the institution notifies the responsible Standesamt and sends the birth certificate from the hospital. For a home birth, the midwife or doctor issues that certificate, and you must present it to the responsible Standesamt within one week.

The Standesamt for the place of birth is the responsible office. Its website lists what other documents it needs.

rows.question: What do we need to bring to the Standesamt to register the birth?
rows.reply:
Under the federal registration regulation, when a birth is reported the Standesamt (civil registry office) "soll … verlangen" (should require) that you present the following (PStV §33):

1. If the parents are married to each other: your marriage certificate or a certified extract from the marriage register. You also need your own birth certificates if the details of your births do not appear on the marriage certificate. The marriage certificate is required even if the marriage has ended.
2. If the parents are not married to each other: the mother's birth certificate. If paternity has already been acknowledged, also the paternity declarations and the father's birth certificate, and any joint custody declarations.
3. An identity card, passport or other recognised passport substitute for the parents.
4. If the birth is reported in person: a certificate of birth issued by the doctor or midwife who was present at the birth.

The Standesamt may ask for further documents where they are needed to prove the details given (PStV §33).

If your child was born in a hospital, birth centre or maternity clinic, the facility notifies the Standesamt and sends it the birth certificate. If your child was born at home, the midwife or doctor issues the birth certificate, and the official family portal says you must present it to the Standesamt within 1 week.

Where the parents are foreign nationals, the Standesamt asks, when the birth is reported, whether a parent holds an unlimited right of residence (or a residence permit under the EU–Switzerland free movement agreement). It then obtains written information from the immigration authority. This is used to check whether the child acquired German citizenship by birth (PStV §34). The Standesamt carries out that check.

The family portal says the further documents you need are listed on the website of the Standesamt in the place where your child is born. That Standesamt is the one responsible for the place of birth.

rows.question: Does my Krankenkasse pay for a midwife?
rows.reply:
The statutory health insurance law gives an insured woman a right to midwife care. Under SGB V §24d, during pregnancy, at the birth and after the birth, she is entitled to medical care and to help from a Hebamme (midwife) ("Anspruch auf ärztliche Betreuung sowie auf Hebammenhilfe"). This includes the examinations to confirm the pregnancy and prenatal check-ups.

After the birth, the right to Hebamme help with postnatal care ("Wochenbettbetreuung") lasts until the end of twelve weeks after the birth ("bis zum Ablauf von zwölf Wochen nach der Geburt"). Further services beyond that need a doctor's order ("bedürfen der ärztlichen Anordnung"). If the mother cannot care for the child after the birth, the insured child has its own right to the Hebamme services that relate to the child.

The Familienportal confirms that every woman with statutory health insurance is entitled to support from a Hebamme. If you have private health insurance instead, it says to check with your insurer beforehand which services it covers.

This states the general rule. Whether a particular service is covered in your case is decided by your Krankenkasse (statutory health insurer), so that is the body to contact.

rows.question: How long after the birth can I still see a midwife at the Krankenkasse's cost?
rows.reply:
Under federal law, a woman insured with a Krankenkasse (statutory health insurer) is entitled to midwife help during pregnancy, at the birth and after the birth. This rule is for women with statutory health insurance. If you are privately insured, the official family portal says you should check with your insurer which services it covers.

rows.question: How do we insure the baby after the birth?
rows.reply:
Under federal law, a baby can be covered through Familienversicherung (free family cover for dependants) under statutory health insurance. SGB V §10 says the children of members are insured ("Versichert sind ... die Kinder von Mitgliedern") if the child meets all five of these conditions: 1. lives or usually stays in Germany; 2. is not compulsorily insured in their own right under the listed provisions, and is not voluntarily insured; 3. is not exempt from insurance and has not been released from compulsory insurance; 4. is not self-employed as their main occupation; 5. has no total income that regularly exceeds one seventh of the monthly reference amount ("ein Siebtel der monatlichen Bezugsgröße"). Children are covered up to their 18th birthday ("bis zur Vollendung des achtzehnten Lebensjahres"), with longer periods in the cases the law lists.

There is an exception. A child is not covered this way if the parent related to the child who is the member's spouse or civil partner is not a member of a statutory health insurance fund, and that parent's total income regularly exceeds one twelfth of the annual earnings ceiling ("ein Zwölftel der Jahresarbeitsentgeltgrenze") and is regularly higher than the member's income.

If the conditions are met through more than one parent, the member chooses the health insurance fund. The member must report the insured child to the responsible health insurance fund, with the details needed to carry out the cover, and must also report later changes to those details.

To do this you need the birth certificate. The family portal lists registration with the health insurance fund as one of the things the birth certificate is needed for. The certificate is issued by the registry office for the place of birth. The portal says the child must be registered there within one week of the birth. If the baby was born in a hospital, birth centre or maternity clinic, that facility notifies the registry office and sends the birth notification.

The excerpts do not cover how a baby is insured if neither parent is in statutory health insurance, or which forms the fund uses. Whether your baby is covered is decided by your statutory health insurance fund; contact the fund the insured parent belongs to.

rows.question: When are the first check-ups for the baby?
rows.reply:
Germany's Kinder-Richtlinie sets out ten early-detection check-ups for children in their first six years. The first ones are:

- U1: "unmittelbar nach der Geburt" (immediately after birth). It should take place within the first 30 minutes after the baby is born ("innerhalb der ersten 30 Minuten nach der Geburt"). If no doctor is present at the birth but a midwife is, the midwife should carry it out.
- U2: 3rd to 10th day of life ("3.-10. Lebenstag"). Tolerance limit: 3rd to 14th day.
- U3: 4th to 5th week of life ("4.-5. Lebenswoche"). Tolerance limit: 3rd to 8th week.
- U4: 3rd to 4th month of life. Tolerance limit: 2nd to 4½th month.
- U5: 6th to 7th month of life. Tolerance limit: 5th to 8th month.
- U6: 10th to 12th month of life. Tolerance limit: 9th to 14th month.

The directive says the check-ups "können nur in den jeweils angegebenen Zeiträumen unter Berücksichtigung folgender Toleranzgrenzen in Anspruch genommen werden". This means each one can only be used within its stated period, allowing for the tolerance limit. The same periods also apply to babies born prematurely ("Auch bei Frühgeborenen sind die Untersuchungszeiträume einzuhalten"). Premature birth is taken into account when the results are assessed.

The later check-ups run up to U9, at 60 to 64 months. Children are entitled to these early-detection check-ups until they turn 18.

rows.question: What is Mutterschaftsgeld and when do I apply for it?
rows.reply:
Mutterschaftsgeld (maternity pay from the health insurer) is a payment for the maternity protection periods before and after the birth, and for the day of the birth itself ("für die Zeit der Schutzfristen vor und nach der Entbindung sowie für den Entbindungstag"). Which rules apply depends on whether you are a member of a statutory health insurer.

If you are a member of a statutory health insurer: you receive Mutterschaftsgeld under the rules of the Fifth Book of the Social Code (MuSchG §19(1)). For members who are employed when the protection period before the birth begins, it equals the average daily net pay of the last three settled calendar months before that period, up to a maximum of 13 euros per calendar day ("höchstens 13 Euro für den Kalendertag"). Pay above 13 euros a day is covered by the employer or by the body responsible for paying Mutterschaftsgeld, under the Maternity Protection Act (SGB V §24i(2)). That employer top-up is set out in MuSchG §20(1). For payment before the birth, a certificate from a doctor or a midwife stating the expected date of delivery is decisive (SGB V §24i(3)). The entitlement is suspended for as long as you receive pay subject to contributions, income from work, or holiday compensation. This does not apply to one-off payments (SGB V §24i(4)).

If you are not a member of a statutory health insurer: Mutterschaftsgeld is paid by the federal government, up to a total of 210 euros ("insgesamt höchstens 210 Euro"). It is paid on application ("auf Antrag") by the Bundesamt für Soziale Sicherung (MuSchG §19(2)).

When the protection periods fall: the Familienportal states that they normally begin 6 weeks before the calculated due date and end 8 weeks after the birth.

When to apply: the excerpts I have do not say when or how to apply. For statutory members, ask your health insurer. If you are not statutorily insured, the Bundesamt für Soziale Sicherung is the body that pays on application. Whether you are entitled, and how much you receive, is decided by that body, not here.

Mutterschaftsgeld is also offset against Elterngeld (BEEG §3(1)). The flat 210 euro payment under MuSchG §19(2) is the exception.

rows.question: We are not married. Is my partner automatically the legal father?
rows.reply:
No. Under German law, being the partner of the mother does not by itself make a man the legal father. BGB §1592 names three ways a man becomes the father of a child. He is the man who, at the time of the birth, is married to the mother ("zum Zeitpunkt der Geburt mit der Mutter des Kindes verheiratet ist"). Or he is the man who has acknowledged paternity ("die Vaterschaft anerkannt hat"). Or he is the man whose paternity has been established by a court ("gerichtlich festgestellt ist").

For parents who are not married at the birth, the official family portal states that the father must make a Vaterschaftsanerkennung (acknowledgement of paternity) to count as the legal father. The acknowledgement is voluntary and needs the mother's consent.

What the law says about the acknowledgement itself (BGB §1594):
- It can be made before the child is born ("schon vor der Geburt des Kindes zulässig").
- It is not effective while another man's paternity exists.
- It is invalid if made subject to a condition or a time limit.
- Its legal effects can generally only be relied on from the moment it becomes effective.

Where it is made: the father must make his declaration in person at a competent office. Examples are your youth welfare office, a registry office, a local court, or a notary. The mother must also give her consent in person. The office records both the father's declaration and the mother's consent. Depending on the federal state, it can cost a fee at a notary or a local court.

Acknowledging paternity does not on its own give the father parental custody. For unmarried parents, the mother has parental custody from the birth. Joint custody also requires both parents to declare that they want joint custody, or a court decision, or the parents marrying after the birth.

Whether these rules have been met in your own case is decided by the office that records the acknowledgement. Your local youth welfare office advises on parental custody.

rows.question: How do unmarried parents get joint custody?
rows.reply:
Under federal law, if the parents are not married to each other when the child is born, the mother has parental custody from birth. The other parent can gain it only if certain conditions are met. Parents get joint custody in any of three ways. The statute lists them in BGB §1626a(1):

1. Both parents declare that they want to take on custody jointly. These declarations are called Sorgeerklärung (declaration of joint custody), plural Sorgeerklärungen ("wenn sie erklären, dass sie die Sorge gemeinsam übernehmen wollen").
2. The parents marry each other ("wenn sie einander heiraten").
3. The family court transfers custody to them jointly ("soweit ihnen das Familiengericht die elterliche Sorge gemeinsam überträgt").

If none of these applies, the mother has custody ("Im Übrigen hat die Mutter die elterliche Sorge").

The court route starts with an application by one parent. The court transfers all or part of custody to both parents if this does not conflict with the child's welfare ("wenn die Übertragung dem Kindeswohl nicht widerspricht"). If the other parent raises no reasons against it, and none are otherwise apparent, the law presumes that joint custody does not conflict with the child's welfare. The federal family portal adds that in this case the family court decides in a simplified procedure. It does so without hearing the youth welfare office and without hearing the parents in person.

According to the federal family portal, the other parent must first be legally recognised as the father. This happens when he acknowledges the child as his own with the mother's consent, or when a court establishes paternity. Recognition of paternity alone does not give him custody. The Sorgeerklärungen or a court decision are still needed.

When Sorgeerklärungen are made, or a court transfers joint custody by a final decision, this is entered in a custody register kept by the responsible youth welfare office (SGB VIII §58).

Unmarried parents have a legal right to advice on making a Sorgeerklärung and on the option of a court transfer of joint custody (SGB VIII §18(2)). The family portal names your local youth welfare office as the place that advises on all questions of parental custody. The excerpts do not say how or where the declarations themselves are made. Your local youth welfare office is the authority to ask about that.

rows.question: Where do we apply for Elterngeld in Frankfurt?
rows.reply:
You apply at the Elterngeldstelle responsible for where your child lives. Under federal law, the federal states decide which authorities carry out Elterngeld (parental allowance). The responsible one is the authority "des Bezirks, in dem das Kind, für das Elterngeld beansprucht wird, zum Zeitpunkt der ersten Antragstellung seinen inländischen Wohnsitz hat". In plain terms, it is the authority for the district where the child is registered as living in Germany when you first apply. The federal family portal says the same: contact the Elterngeldstelle for your child's place of residence.

In Hessen, the Regierungspräsidium Gießen's Elterngeld page lists current contact details for the six Hessian offices for welfare and social affairs. It also names the supervisory body for Elterngeld at the Regierungspräsidium Gießen. The excerpts do not say which of the six offices covers Frankfurt. Use the contact list on that page to find the office for your child's district.

How to apply: Elterngeld must be applied for in writing ("schriftlich zu beantragen"). According to the family portal, you can apply in person at an Elterngeldstelle or online. Digital applications are possible in every federal state.

Timing matters. Payment is made retroactively only for the last three months of the child's life before the month in which the application is received. Earlier months are not paid.

rows.question: Where do we apply for Elterngeld in Berlin?
rows.reply:

In Berlin there are two electronic routes:
- ElterngeldDigital is available in Berlin. A digital assistant helps you fill in the application. You then print the document, sign it and send it by post to your responsible Elterngeldstelle.
- Berlin's service portal describes an online application. To use it, you log in with a BundID account, or register for one if you do not have one. The page recommends an activated online ID function (eID), such as on an electronic residence permit (eAT). An Elster certificate or username and password are alternatives.

rows.question: Will our baby automatically be German if we are both Indian citizens?
rows.reply:
Not automatically in every case. German law sets two separate routes to German Staatsangehörigkeit (citizenship) at birth, and which one could apply depends on conditions only the authorities check.

By descent: a child acquires German Staatsangehörigkeit at birth if one parent holds German Staatsangehörigkeit ("wenn ein Elternteil die deutsche Staatsangehörigkeit besitzt").

By birth in Germany to foreign parents: a child of foreign parents born in Germany acquires German Staatsangehörigkeit if one parent meets both of these conditions:
1. has had lawful habitual residence in Germany for five years ("seit fünf Jahren rechtmäßig seinen gewöhnlichen Aufenthalt im Inland hat"), and
2. holds an unlimited right of residence ("ein unbefristetes Aufenthaltsrecht"), or, as a Swiss citizen or a Swiss citizen's family member, a residence permit under the 1999 EU–Switzerland free movement agreement.
Only one parent needs to meet both conditions. The acquisition is entered in the birth register where the child's birth is recorded.

Who decides: when the birth is registered, the registry office asks whether a parent has an unlimited right of residence. It then obtains written information from the foreigners' authority on whether this is correct and whether the parent had five years of lawful habitual residence in Germany at the time of the birth. The registry office then checks whether the child acquired German Staatsangehörigkeit by birth and records the result. Whether your child acquires it is decided there, not here.

If a child born in Germany does not acquire German Staatsangehörigkeit, the residence law has a separate rule: if both parents hold a residence permit, a settlement permit or an EU long-term residence permit at the time of birth, the child is granted a residence permit ex officio. If only one parent holds one, a residence permit can be granted. If a parent holds a visa or may stay visa-free at the birth, the child's stay counts as permitted until that visa or visa-free stay ends. Your local foreigners' authority is responsible for residence matters.

The excerpts do not cover Indian citizenship rules for the child. For that, contact the Indian consular mission responsible for your area.

rows.question: Does our newborn need a residence permit?
rows.reply:
The law sets out several situations for a child born in Germany. Which one applies to your child depends on the parents' own status, and that is decided by the authorities, not here.

An Aufenthaltserlaubnis (residence permit) for the child (AufenthG §33):
- If one parent holds "eine Aufenthaltserlaubnis, eine Niederlassungserlaubnis oder eine Erlaubnis zum Daueraufenthalt – EU", the child born in Germany may be granted an Aufenthaltserlaubnis by the authority on its own initiative ("kann ... von Amts wegen ... erteilt werden").
- If, at the time of birth, both parents, or the parent who alone has custody, hold one of those titles, the child is granted the Aufenthaltserlaubnis on the authority's own initiative ("wird ... von Amts wegen erteilt").
- If the mother or father holds a visa at the time of birth, or is allowed to stay without a visa, the child's stay counts as permitted until that visa or lawful visa-free stay ends ("gilt bis zum Ablauf des Visums oder des rechtmäßigen visumfreien Aufenthalts als erlaubt").

German citizenship by birth (StAG §4):
- A child acquires German citizenship by birth if one parent is a German citizen (§4(1)).
- A child of foreign parents born in Germany acquires German citizenship if one parent has lawfully had their habitual residence in Germany for five years ("seit fünf Jahren rechtmäßig seinen gewöhnlichen Aufenthalt im Inland") and holds an unlimited right of residence ("ein unbefristetes Aufenthaltsrecht") or, as a Swiss citizen or family member of one, a residence permit under the EU–Switzerland free movement agreement (§4(3)).
- When the birth is registered, the Standesamt (civil registry office) asks whether a parent holds such a right, obtains a written statement from the Ausländerbehörde (foreigners' authority) on whether the details are correct, and examines whether the child acquired German citizenship by birth (PStV §34).

The excerpts do not set out how to apply for the child's permit or which forms are used. Whether your child falls under any of these rules is decided by the authorities, not by this answer. For the child's residence status, your local Ausländerbehörde is the responsible office; the check on German citizenship at birth is made by the Standesamt that registers the birth.

rows.question: We are getting Mutterschaftsgeld. Does that reduce our Elterngeld?
rows.reply:
Yes. Under federal law, Mutterschaftsgeld (maternity pay from the health insurer) is credited against Elterngeld (parental allowance). The statute says these benefits "werden angerechnet" (are credited) on the Elterngeld.

What the law lists (BEEG §3(1) No. 1):
- Mutterschaftsgeld under the Fifth Book of the Social Code (statutory health insurance) or the farmers' health insurance law.
- The employer's supplement to Mutterschaftsgeld under MuSchG §20.

Both are credited only for the period "ab dem Tag der Geburt des Kindes" (from the day of the child's birth).

One exception: the Mutterschaftsgeld paid under MuSchG §19(2) is not credited. That is the payment for women who are not members of a statutory health insurer, "insgesamt höchstens 210 Euro" (at most 210 euros in total), paid by the Bundesamt für Soziale Sicherung.

The 300-euro amount in BEEG §3(2) that is otherwise free from crediting does not protect against maternity benefits. It applies "soweit nicht Einnahmen nach Absatz 1 Satz 1 Nummer 1 bis 3" are credited, and maternity benefits are Number 1.

If maternity benefits cover only part of a month of the child's life, they are credited only against the matching part of that month's Elterngeld (BEEG §3(1)).

The federal family portal adds the following for benefits received for the same child:
- If the maternity benefits are higher than the Elterngeld, only the maternity benefits are paid. If the Elterngeld is higher, the difference is paid as Elterngeld.
- Months in which maternity benefits are received for the same child "gelten bei Ihnen als Monate mit Basiselterngeld" (count as months of basic Elterngeld). One day of entitlement in that month is enough.
- Maternity benefits are credited only against the mother's Elterngeld, not against the father's.

What this means for your own payments is decided by the Elterngeldstelle responsible for your district.

rows.question: Can I work while receiving Elterngeld?
rows.reply:
Yes, the law allows it within limits. Elterngeld (parental allowance) is available to a person who does no paid work or does not work full time: "keine oder keine volle Erwerbstätigkeit ausübt" (BEEG §1(1) no. 4).

Under BEEG §1(6), a person counts as not fully employed if any one of these applies:
1. their working time does not exceed 32 hours a week on average over the child's month of life ("32 Wochenstunden im Durchschnitt des Lebensmonats");
2. they are in employment for vocational training ("Beschäftigung zur Berufsbildung");
3. they work as a suitably qualified childminder within the meaning of §§ 23 and 43 of Book VIII of the Social Code.

Working affects the amount. For months after the birth in which you earn less than before the birth, Elterngeld is paid as the applicable percentage of the difference between the two incomes. For this comparison, pre-birth income counts up to at most 2,770 euros (BEEG §2(3)). The maximum of 1,800 euros a month applies to full months with no income from work (BEEG §2(1)).

The law also lets you take two months of the Plus variant ("Elterngeld Plus") instead of one month of basic Elterngeld (BEEG §4(3)).

If your application says you expect to earn during the payment period, the amount is decided provisionally. After the payment period ends, you must prove your actual income from work for that time (BEEG §8(1) and (3)). If your application says you expect no income from work, Elterngeld is paid subject to revocation in case you do earn (BEEG §8(2)).

Whether you qualify, and how much you would receive, is decided only by the Elterngeld office responsible for your district.

rows.question: Where and how do we apply for Kindergeld?
rows.reply:
Kindergeld (child benefit) must be applied for in writing. The law says the application "ist schriftlich zu beantragen" and should be made to the responsible Familienkasse (BKGG §9(1)).

Where: the responsible Familienkasse is the one for the district where the entitled person has their residence ("Wohnsitz"). That office both receives the application and decides on the claim (BKGG §13(1)). The federal family portal tells you to submit the application to the Familienkasse of your Agentur für Arbeit.

How, according to the federal family portal:
- Use the Familienkassen's form. You can fill it in online, then print and sign it.
- For newborn children, you can apply fully online with a valid ELSTER certificate. You then do not need to print or sign by hand.
- The application must include your tax identification number and your child's tax identification number.
- For questions about applying, the Bundesagentur für Arbeit has a free service line: 0800 4 555530.

Who applies: Kindergeld is paid to only one person per child (BKGG §3(1)). If the child lives in the parents' shared household, the parents decide between themselves who is the entitled person (BKGG §3(2)). Besides the entitled person, anyone with a legitimate interest in the payment may also apply (BKGG §9(1)).

Whether you are entitled is decided by the Familienkasse for your district.

rows.question: What are the Elterngeld rules for a self-employed parent in Bavaria?
rows.reply:
Elterngeld (parental allowance) is federal law, so the rules below apply in Bavaria as everywhere in Germany. Bavaria itself is outside the states this product covers (federal law, Hessen, and the Indian consular track), so its application procedures, forms and offices are not covered here. For those, contact the Elterngeld office responsible in Bavaria or the Bavarian state government's official portal.

What the federal law says about self-employed parents:

1. Self-employed income counts. The income Elterngeld is based on includes positive income from "Land- und Forstwirtschaft, Gewerbebetrieb und selbständiger Arbeit" (agriculture and forestry, trade or business, and self-employment), as well as employment income, in each case taxable in Germany and reduced by deductions for taxes and social contributions (BEEG §2(1)). The rules in BEEG §2c that were provided cover employment income only. The excerpts do not include the provision that sets out how self-employed income is worked out, so that is not covered here.

2. Amount rules. Elterngeld is 67 percent of pre-birth earned income, up to 1,800 euros a month for full months with no earned income. The percentage rises toward 100 percent where pre-birth income was below 1,000 euros, and falls to as low as 65 percent where it was above 1,200 euros. The minimum is 300 euros, even with no pre-birth earned income (BEEG §2(1), (2), (4)). If you earn less after the birth than before, Elterngeld is paid on the difference, with pre-birth income counted at no more than 2,770 euros (BEEG §2(3)).

3. Working while receiving it. A person must not be in full employment. A person is not fully employed if working time does not exceed 32 hours a week on average over the month of the child's life (BEEG §1(1) No. 4, §1(6)). People who are "selbständig erwerbstätig" (self-employed) count as employed even while they are temporarily not working (BEEG §1(6a)).

4. Provisional decisions. The amount is decided provisionally, based on the information made credible, if any of these apply: (1) at the time of application the tax assessment for the last completed tax period before the birth is not yet available and it cannot yet be stated whether the 175,000 euro limit is exceeded; (2) pre-birth earned income cannot be determined; or (3) the applicant expects to have earned income during the payment period (BEEG §8(3)). Where projected earned income was given in the application, actual income for that period must be proven after the payment period ends (BEEG §8(1)).

5. Income limit. The entitlement lapses if taxable income in the last completed tax period before the birth was more than 175,000 euros, or, where another person also qualifies, if both persons' combined taxable income was more than 175,000 euros (BEEG §1(8)).

Whether you qualify and how much you would receive is decided only by the responsible Elterngeld office, not here.

rows.question: Can you fill in our Elterngeld application form for us?
rows.reply:
I cannot fill in your application. The form asks for your own details and your own choices, and only the responsible authority decides your individual case. Here is what the law says the application must contain.

Elterngeld (parental allowance) must be applied for in writing ("ist schriftlich zu beantragen"). The application must state for which months of the child's life you claim basic parental allowance, for which months parental allowance plus, and for which months the partnership bonus. (BEEG §7(1))

The person applying signs the application. The other eligible parent also signs it to confirm they have seen it. This does not apply where the applicant has sole custody or in the case of §4c. The other parent may, at the same time, make their own application or tell the authority how many monthly amounts they claim. If the authority has neither from the other parent, all monthly amounts are paid to the parent who applied. The other parent can then only receive what remains of the joint entitlement. (BEEG §7(3))

Payment is made retroactively only for the last three months of the child's life before the month in which the application is received. Earlier months are not paid. (BEEG §7(1))

The choices made in the application can be changed until the end of the payment period. A change can apply retroactively only to the last three months before the month the change request is received. It is not allowed for months already paid out, except in cases of special hardship. (BEEG §7(2))

The official family portal lists documents to attach, including your child's birth certificate and proof of your previous income. (familienportal.de)

The authority responsible is the one your Land designates for Elterngeld in the district where your child lives at the time of the first application (BEEG §12(1)). Contact that office for your district for the form and for questions about your own case.

rows.question: Based on our situation, will our Elterngeld application be approved?
rows.reply:
Whether your application will be approved is an individual decision. This service cannot assess it or predict the outcome. Only the Elterngeldstelle for your district decides your case. It is the authority whose decision on Elterngeld (parental allowance) can be challenged by objection.

What the law says, for everyone:

Basic conditions (BEEG §1(1)). A person is entitled to Elterngeld if they meet all four of these:
1. They have a residence or habitual stay in Germany.
2. They live in one household with their child.
3. They care for and bring up the child themselves.
4. They work not at all, or not full time.

A person is not working full time if any one of these applies (BEEG §1(6)):
- Their working time does not exceed "32 Wochenstunden im Durchschnitt des Lebensmonats" (32 hours a week, averaged over the month).
- They are in vocational training.
- They work as a suitable childminder.

Residence status (BEEG §1(7)). A non-EU national who does not have free-movement rights is only entitled in one of these cases:
1. They hold a settlement permit or an EU long-term residence permit.
2. They hold an EU Blue Card, an ICT card, a Mobile ICT card, or a residence permit that permits work for a period of "mindestens sechs Monaten" (at least six months). There are exceptions for permits issued for certain purposes, such as training, au-pair or seasonal work, study, job-seeking, and certain humanitarian grounds.
3. They hold one of those humanitarian permits and work lawfully, take parental leave, or receive ongoing benefits under the Third Book of the Social Code.
4. They hold one of those humanitarian permits and have stayed in Germany lawfully, with permission, or tolerated for at least 15 months.
5. They hold an employment toleration (Beschäftigungsduldung).

Income limit (BEEG §1(8)). The entitlement lapses if taxable income in the last completed assessment period before the birth was "mehr als 175 000 Euro" (more than 175,000 euros). If another person also qualifies as a parent in the household, the same limit applies to the two incomes combined.

Minimum period (BEEG §4(4)). A parent is only entitled if they receive Elterngeld for at least two months of the child's life.

Application (BEEG §7(1)). Elterngeld must be applied for in writing. Payment is made retroactively only for the last three months of the child's life before the month in which the application is received. Earlier months are not paid.

For a decision on your own situation, approach the Elterngeldstelle for your district.

rows.question: How much tax will we save if I switch to Steuerklasse 3 before the birth?
rows.reply:
How much tax you would save by switching tax class is a calculation for your family's own situation. This service cannot make it. Tax class choice and its tax effects belong to a tax adviser or your local tax office.

The excerpts do cover how a tax class change before the birth affects parental allowance:

- The federal family portal says a tax class change before the birth "kann sich ... auf die Höhe Ihrer Steuern und Ihrer Sozialabgaben auswirken" (can affect the level of your taxes and social contributions).
- For the simplified net-income calculation behind parental allowance, the newest tax class counts. The older tax class is used only if it applied for longer than the newer one within the whole assessment period.
- Changing tax class again after the birth no longer has any effect on parental allowance.
- For employment income, the assessment period is the twelve calendar months before the month of the birth ("die zwölf Kalendermonate vor dem Kalendermonat der Geburt des Kindes"). Some months are left out of that period. These include the maternity protection periods and months of illness mainly caused by the pregnancy.
- The law deducts income tax according to the tax class, and tax class VI is not taken into account ("die Steuerklasse VI bleibt unberücksichtigt").

Which tax class counts for your parental allowance, and the amount, are decided by the parental allowance office for your district. The tax effect of switching is a question for a tax adviser or your local tax office.
